data.one_liner: Cross-platform API to check and request permissions on iOS, Android, Web, and Windows.
data.what_it_does: Provides a unified cross-platform API to request and check runtime permissions such as camera, contacts, location, and storage. It also allows developers to open the device's app settings and handle rationales on Android.
use_when: Your app needs to access device features requiring runtime permissions (camera, location, contacts, etc.)
You need to check permission status or send users to the system settings page to grant permissions manually.
avoid_when: You are targeting platforms where permissions are entirely handled automatically at install time without runtime checks.
strengths: Supports multiple platforms including iOS, Android, Web, and Windows.
Provides granular permission control and status checking.
Handles OS-specific permission macros and requirements.
weaknesses: Requires manual configuration in native files like AndroidManifest.xml and iOS Info.plist / Podfile / SPM settings.
Changes in native platform permission behavior require careful handling of request-driven patterns.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding specific permission configurations and usage descriptions to AndroidManifest.xml and iOS Info.plist, along with optional Podfile preprocessor definitions or Swift Package Manager settings.

alternatives.name: app_settings
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need to open specific application settings screens rather than a full permission management solution.
